Introducing Product is the complete **Introducing remocn** video, shipped as
editable React source. The default render is a 32-second launch video at
1920×1080 and 60 fps, with nine scenes and an original instrumental soundtrack.

The install includes every scene, motion presets, content, theme, and soundtrack
source. It also installs the `word-push` and `radial-burst` primitives used in the
live demonstrations, plus Manrope font files through `@fontsource/manrope`.
The default video makes no external asset or API requests.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Composition } from "remotion";
import {
  IntroducingProduct,
  INTRODUCING_DURATION,
  INTRODUCING_FPS,
  INTRODUCING_WIDTH,
  INTRODUCING_HEIGHT,
} from "@/components/remocn/templates/introducing-product";

export const RemotionRoot = () => (
  <Composition
    id="IntroducingProduct"
    component={IntroducingProduct}
    durationInFrames={INTRODUCING_DURATION * INTRODUCING_FPS}
    fps={INTRODUCING_FPS}
    width={INTRODUCING_WIDTH}
    height={INTRODUCING_HEIGHT}
    defaultProps={{}}
  />
);
```

Render with your existing Remotion entry:

```bash
npx remotion render IntroducingProduct out/introducing-product.mp4 --codec=h264 --crf=16
```

In the remocn repository, use `bun run studio:introducing` to open the dedicated
composition or `bun run render:introducing` to export `out/introducing-remocn.mp4`.

## Make it yours

```tsx
<IntroducingProduct
  productName="Forma"
  website="forma.example"
  accentColor="#B7D7FA"
  content={{
    hook: "You have the idea.",
    hookPayoff: "Give it a shape.",
    tagline: "Your next idea, beautifully made.",
    installCommand: "npm create forma@latest",
    installLabel: "Start with one command.",
    galleryTitle: "A better starting point.",
    initialText: "Your first idea.",
    editedText: "Your next launch.",
    showcaseTitle: "Made with Forma.",
    showcaseWords: ["Imagine.", "Create.", "Share."],
    ownershipTitle: "Your idea. Your creation.",
    closingLine: "Make something worth sharing.",
  }}
/>
```

Changing the product name replaces the remocn mark with an initial mark. Supply
`logoSrc` to use a real logo. Product-specific demonstrations are source scenes:
replace the code editor and component previews when your product works differently.

The preview controls cover product name, URL, accent, sound, and volume. The
remaining content and scene layout are edited through props or source files.
The complete timeline stays 32 seconds; motion is calculated in seconds, so
30 fps exports also work when the composition duration is set to `32 * 30`.

| Prop | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `productName` | `"remocn"` | Name throughout the film; overrides `content.productName` |
| `website` | `"remocn.dev"` | Final URL; overrides `content.website` |
| `accentColor` | `"#D4B3FF"` | Main accent; overrides `theme.accent` |
| `logoSrc` | — | Image URL or `staticFile(...)` path; otherwise a vector/initial mark |
| `content` | remocn copy | Partial override of the exported `introducingContent` object |
| `theme` | graphite, paper, lavender, peach, mint | Partial override of `introducingTheme`; six-digit hex colors |
| `sound` | `true` | Include the original score or replacement audio |
| `audioSrc` | generated original score | Replacement audio URL or `staticFile(...)` path |
| `volume` | `0.8` | Audio volume, clamped to 0–1 |

Use concise titles (roughly 3–7 words), a short tagline, and a readable install
command. Main titles and names scale down to fit; very long strings will become
small. Blank content fields and missing array entries use their defaults. The
composition is designed for 16:9; other aspect ratios are letterboxed. Redesign
scene positions for a native portrait edit.

## Scene source

| Time | File | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0–2.5 s | `scenes/hook.tsx` | Short word-driven opening |
| 2.5–5 s | `scenes/brand.tsx` | Mark and product reveal |
| 5–9 s | `scenes/install.tsx` | Command becomes a live preview |
| 9–13 s | `scenes/gallery.tsx` | Components fan into a gallery |
| 13–18 s | `scenes/customize.tsx` | Color, copy, and timing change in source and preview |
| 18–22 s | `scenes/compose.tsx` | Preview cards gather into timeline clips |
| 22–26 s | `scenes/showcase.tsx` | A finished mini launch sequence fills the screen |
| 26–29 s | `scenes/ownership.tsx` | Ownership statement resolves to the mark |
| 29–32 s | `scenes/outro.tsx` | Brand and URL hold |

`index.tsx` owns the composition. `content.ts` owns copy and theme defaults.
`motion.ts` owns the timeline and named easing curves. `shared.tsx` contains the
brand mark, type helpers, cursor, and window chrome. `previews.tsx` contains live
component demonstrations. Scene components remain ordinary React functions:
replace, reorder, or extend them to match your story.

If you change scene durations, update the `from` times, total duration, any
shared transition geometry, and soundtrack accents together. The generated
score is composed for the default 32-second edit.

## Sound and assets

The default instrumental and transition accents are synthesized by
`soundtrack.ts`, with no third-party samples. This source is MIT-licensed with
the template. The score is cached after its first generation and packaged as a
WAV data URI for both the Player and MP4 renderer.

For a silent export, pass `sound={false}`. To replace the score:

```tsx
import { staticFile } from "remotion";

<IntroducingProduct
  audioSrc={staticFile("launch-score.wav")}
  volume={0.7}
/>
```

Put replacement media in your project's `public/` folder. Supply a track long
enough for the composition. Missing or inaccessible custom assets should be
fixed before rendering; they are not silently replaced by unrelated media.
